maintopic: REPORTED INCREASE IN CUSTOMS DUTIES

speechtext: On the Orders of the Day:

maintopic: REPORTED INCREASE IN CUSTOMS DUTIES
speechtext:
I desire to direct the attention of the Government, and of the Finance Minister (Sir Henry Drayton) in particular, to a statement sent out by one of the larger New York banks to its Canadian correspondents, and by them passed along to their branches throughout Canada, intimating that the New York hank has information that the Canadian Government will, within a very short time, increase the customs duties by adding 30 per cent to the already existing duties.
I am sure that if this information is not well-founded, the Government and the Finance Minister will see the importance of at once giving it a flat denial; otherwise, it will stimulate imports that are not immediately needed. On the other hand, if it is well-founded, someone has been indiscreet.

speakerposition: Secretary of State of Canada; Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: REPORTED INCREASE IN CUSTOMS DUTIES
speechtext: I thank the hon. member for bringing the matter to my attention. This is the very first I have heard of it. My hon. friend is well aware that it would be entirely improper for us to make any declarations on the subject matter of the report one way or the other, at the present time. I may say, however, that the imposition of an additional 30 per cent is not even being considered.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS

speechtext:
On motion of Rt. Hon. Sir George Foster (Minister of Trade and Commerce) Bill No. 13 to amend and consolidate the Acts respecting the Inpection of Gas and Gas Meters, was read the second time, and the House went into Committee thereon, Mr. Boivin in the Chair.
On section 2-definitions:

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: This Bill is both to amend and to consolidate different Acts. Perhaps my hon. friend would direct the attention of the Committee to any amending features when they are not apparent from the Bill itself.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I will do that as we pass along. Some amendments are introduced, and consolidation has taken place. It was thought better to consolidate the old Acts and make the amendments at the same time so that it would be all under the one cover.

Section agreed to.
On section 3-regulations:

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I move that
clause 3 be amended by adding thereto, as paragraph (g), the following words: "as to pressure under which gas is to be supplied." That is at present in the old Act, but it was omitted in the printing of the new.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
In the old Act I find these words, immediately following those which my hon. friend has just moved to insert as paragraph (g):
In the case of inodorous gas, to require the addition of such substances as he deems necessary in order to communicate the odor.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: In the old Act there is such a clause as my hon. friend has mentioned; I do not know just why it has been left out of this Bill. My officer is on his way here; we will let the clause stand until we get an explanation from him.

Amendment agreed to.
Section stands.
On section 4-units of measure:

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Does
paragraph 2 have reference to natural gas as supplied to consumers in different parts in Canada?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
The Bill deals
with both natural and manufactured gas.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: What provision is made for the testing of natural gas?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
We shall come
to that a little later.

Section agreed to.
On section 5-certificate of registration:

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: This is a new clause so far as inspection of gas is concerned, but old as regards electricity. It is considered necessary to apply to the supplying of gas the inspection provision which has worked so well with regard to electrical supply. The certificates are furnished free of charge, and are for the period of a year. They have a statistical value as well, because you know then who are engaged in the work of supplying gas and are able to keep the business under supervision, which you could not do if you did not have the system of registration.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Will this legislation be retroactive? Will it apply to companies already in existence?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: It has no retroactive effect.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
But it must apply to companies already in existence, for it says:
No distribution system for supplying: gas to any purchaser shall he operated until the contractor has obtained from the minister a certificate of registration for such system.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: It is not retroactive; it does not operate until the Bill becomes law, but when the Bill does become law the certificate will be asked for from that date.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Take the case of Three Rivers, where the system of gas distribution has been in operation for some time and under very varying conditions. We have had natural gas and we have had artificial gas, and I do not think that anyone in the town could make any accurate report on the system, because it is not known where the pipes are. If the provision has reference to the manner in which the gas is manufactured, whether with coal or with sawdust, well and good.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: All it requires is that the company or person operating the distribution system shall get a certificate of registration. You cannot carry on your inspection system unless you know what persons or companies are operating the different systems.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: That is, every* gas company must register with the department?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Yes.
Mr. MARCIL.: For a couple of months last winter the gas supplied in Montreal was very bad and complaints poured into the City Hall every day. The company replied that the coal was inferior. Is there in this Bill anything to prevent a repetition of that state of affairs?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I do not quite know what brought about that state of affairs. The department has to do with the inspection of gas; I do not think it has anything to do with looking out for supplies of coal or the finances of a company or anything of that kind. This is merely to see that the gas which is distributed, is measured under proper regulations, so that the consumer shall get his benefit and the contractor or supplier shall be under the regulations and rules of the department.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Did the department receive any complaints from Montreal last winter in regard to the quality of the gas supplied and, if so, did the department take any action? The gas gave out a very bad smell; in fact, in some places we had to cease using the gas entirely on account of its inferior quality. Is any power taken in this Bill to prevent a repetition of that ktate of affairs?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The impurity of gases and the bad quality of gases come directly under the department and we have penalties and fines which may be imposed. The matter is now being attended to in the courts.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: We have a number of companies distributing natural gas in cities and towns in the western part of Ontario, and at times the gas that is supplied is mixed with a large quantity of air. While the gas meters are supplying the people who own the gas wells with the means of taxing the consumer, on the other hand, the consumer is compelled to pay for a very inferior quality of gas. I do not see in the Bill any provision whereby the consumer is sufficiently protected in that regard. The same thing would apply in connection with gas supplied to cities, as has been stated by my hon. friend (Mr. Marcil).

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I am informed that natural gas is not purified by any steps which are taken by the department and it is very difficult to do that.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: What protection is there in the Bill for the consumer of natural gas?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: That seems to be a matter between the contractor and the purchaser. Natural gas is sold as it comes from the soil, and the question whether it is or is not good, and of a quality to fulfil the expectations of the purchaser must, to a large extent, be a matter of bargain between the purchaser and the supplier.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I am sorry indeed there is not in the Bill some provision whereby consumers of natural gas are protected against the men who supply the gas. While it is true that at certain periods of the year, the gas furnished to consumers in western Ontario in particular is of very good quality, yet when there is a shortage of that gas, the general impression is that a large proportion of the material that is furnished through the meters is air which is allowed to be pumped into the pipe lines. I should like to see some protection of the consumer of natural gas, if that is at all possible.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
What effect would the presence of air in the pipes have on gas? I do not know anything about natural gas, but I know something about coal gas.
Mr. ARMSTRONG, (Lambton East): It simply passes through the meter and is registered as gas, although it is merely air which, when it is placed under your furnace or in your stove, does not produce very much heat.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The former legislation which we are amending today made no provision for that, and it is not considered that it is really possible to do so under our Constitution.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: What is required by the department from the contractor in order that he may receive a certificate?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: He must give the information that he is a distributor of gas, the number of his meters, and a general idea as to his system of distribution.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Will the minister be good enough to request his officials to investigate this matter in order to see if it is not possible to devise some legislation whereby consumers of natural gas will be sufficiently protected ?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I shall be very glad to do that.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Why is an annual certificate required? Business men, as a rule, like to have as little interference as possible, and if they receive a certificate when things are going along well, with no complaints from the inspector, why should they be kept under observation every year and compelled to take out a new certificate?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: There is not much trouble in getting or in giving a certificate. The questions which have to be answered are very few and simple; but the department wants to know quite as much as those who go out of the business as the new ones who come into it. Therefore, if you have the expiry of the certificate at the end of each year, you know exactly how many have gone out of the business; and if you require a certificate from everyone doing business, you know all the new ones who come in. In that way your record is complete, and the interference with the business or the trouble given to the firm or association is practically nil.	.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: There seems to be no particular reason why this matter is not left in the hands of the provinces, because a province can grant a charter to a company to distribute gas or electricity. I should like to know if there is any special reason why the federal authorities are interfering in this matter.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: This has been the practice since Confederation, since the first establishment of these two branches I can see very evident advantages which would come from having a capable general supervisory power, and it would be fair to assume, I think, that you would get a better supervisory power from the federal department which devotes its time to the whole Dominion, and can bring about uniformity of work and uniform protection' for the citizens.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: If this condition has existed since Confederation, I do not see whj the section is marked "New."

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Weights and
Measures certainly come under the federal jurisdiction, and this is simply a device for measuring or weighing gas.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: What would be the penalty for failing to apply for this certificate?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
We will come
to that section later.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
My right hon. friend in answer to a question put by my hon.



friend (Mr. Cahill) or my hon. friend (Mr. McKenzie) rather indicated that the obtaining of this certificate of registration was largely a matter of form. If that be the fact, I would point out that the language of the section itself indicates that it goes somewhat beyond that. It says:
No distribution system for supplying gas to any purchaser shall be operated until the contractor has obtained from the minister a certificate of registration for such system.
Assuming that an application was made and the certificate refused, obviously under . this section no person could proceed to distribute under any particular system. That being obvious, what I would like to know is, what is the practical application of the section? Is it optional with the department to refuse such a certificate, or has the department some standard up to which all systems must measure or what regulations in the department have to be complied with before such certificate can be issued? Obviously, if this section were to be strictly interpreted, a person might be prohibited from doing business altogether.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
That is very
true. It is really one of the objects of the Act, that inefficient systems which are not scientific in their nature, or not correct in their working, shall not be operated to the disadvantage of consumers, who have to pay according to the meter readings. It is for the purpose of protecting the consumers from inefficient or deficient methods of distribution. The department has to satisfy itself that the system is reasonably efficient for distribution, and that under that particular system the purchaser of gas will get the service that is reasonably due.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: May I inquire if there are certain fixed standards or regulations in the department that are well known to people engaged in this business?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I am informed by the officer that the purpose of this section is mainly statistical, so that the department shall know who are and who are not doing business. The certificates are generally granted as a matter of course when application is made, and the information obtained is filed.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Having regard to the
explanation just given by my right hon. friend, does he not think that the language of this section is a little too rigid?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: It merely asks that a certificate be granted.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: But it leaves it optional with the department to refuse to grant the certificate, and without the certificate a person cannot carry on business.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I am told that exactly the same provision has been in the Electrical Inspection Act, and that no trouble has ever been found.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I would suggest that if the object of this section is merely that the department shall know who are and who are not doing business in Canada, it ought to be changed, because at present it provides that no system shall be operated until the contractor has first obtained a certificate. That is too drastic, as my hon. friend (Mr. Murphy) says. If the object of the section is mainly statistical, why not draft the clause to read that every contractor supplying gas shall obtain a certificate under a penalty; but do not stop the system just because he does not get a certificate. Under this section, as it stands, if a man in Three Rivers, or in Ottawa, or anywhere else, did not get a certificate, some over-zealous officer in the department could come down and close his plant. That is too drastic. If we are going to legislate as to the quality of gas and provide remedies where a bad quality of gas is being distributed, let us have another clause drafted. But this one exposes even the consumer to hardship.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
It is not the
intention of this clause to interfere with systems already existing and distributing gas, but that every new company shall get a certificate of registration, and that thereafter these certificates shall be supplied yearly in order that a complete statistical record may be kept of what companies are doing business.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: If that is the object, we ought to say "No distribution system for supplying gas hereafter installed or established," and so on. As the section reads now, all existing distributing systems are included, and the supply of gas could be cut off if a certificate was not obtained.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
This clause covers a question that has been a very troublesome one in some parts of the country during the past winter, where companies had threatened to shut off the gas supply to some of their patrons, who had objected to the very great increase in the price of gas charged by the company in violation of contracts made with certain towns. I was not

aware that it was necessary for the companies to receive a certificate of registration annually from the department, but that being the case, I can see the danger of having the supply entirely cut off in case the certificate is refused. A great many people in western Ontario use this natural gas for heating their houses, and if a license is not to be issued, then some means should be provided to see that the supply he maintained so that these people shall not suffer seriously as a result. Many people have no other heating facilities than natural gas. With regard to the question of the impurities of natural gas, the difficulty in certain towns in western Ontario during the past winter has been that companies have refused to purify the gas as they had contracted to do. As this Bill is endeavouring to regulate the gas companies, some provision should be embodied in it to ensure the purity of the gas, and also that, in the event of a certificate being refused a company, some means should be provided to see that the supply is maintained and that the consumer does not suffer.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Possibly my
hon. friend did not hear the slight conversation that passed between another hon. gentleman and myself with reference to natural gas, in the course of which I stated that none of our legislation preceding this had undertaken to look after the purification of natural gas. It is a very difficult^ thing to do, and I promised my hon. friend to have my officers look into the matter to see whether there was any possible method of doing it. The matter will have to rest there for the present. The difficulties which my hon. friend has stated I have seen discussed in the newspapers and in representations made from various quarters, as to the poor quality of natural gas. I must say that we -have not yet legislated in that direction; heretofore the department has considered it so difficult that it has not undertaken to do that work.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I was particularly interested in the fact that these companies require an annual license, and I was anxious to know what would happen if that certificate were not granted and a company were unable to do business, especially in the middle of winter when their customers depend almost entirely on the supply of natural gas. If the company were refused this certificate, what machinery is there to insure the supply to those
39i
who depend upon this gas for their heating purposes?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
The purpose
of this clause is merely to get statistics into the hands of the department. It is not its purpose at all to refuse a certificate because of the quality of the gas, the defects of the system, or anything of that kind. ' The purpose of this clause, I repeat, is simply statistical.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
In view of what my
hon. friend says and obviously intends to do, would it not be better to amend the wording of the section so as to provide that every distribution system shall file with the department so and so, whatever the regulations are, upon which filing the certificates shall issue?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
The objection to
clause 5 as urged on this side of the House as well as on the other, seems to be the apprehension that it will stop the operation of gas companies altogether, with some embarrassment to those who are receiving gas. I would suggest that the minister change the clause so as to read:
Every system supplying gas to any purchaser shall obtain from the minister a certificate of registration for such system, such certificate to expire on the 31st day of March each year.
That would compel them to get a certificate while it would not interfere with their operations. Section 13 says the contractor is penalized if he does not get the certificate.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: If he does not get his registered certificate.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Under clause 5,
which says that no distribution system for supplying gas "shall be operated until the contractor has obtained from the minister a certificate of registration," prevents him from operating if he fails to get the certificate. I do not think it is the intention of the minister to interfere with the operations of these gas concerns, but only to subject them to a penalty for failure to obtain the certificates. I think therefore that the clause is open to amendment.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
My hon. friend is right in the statement that it is not the intention to stop the operation of any gas system by reason of failure to obtain the certificate. The purpose of the clause is simply to compel the contractor to obtain his certificate, so that you may know that he is at work. The penalty in clause 13 is imposed for failure to get registration.

The certificate of registration is really given as a matter of course.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I think clause 5 ought to be amended in accordance with the suggestion of my hon. friend (Mr. McKenzie).

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Section 5 is not intended to prevent operation at all; it merely requires registration.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: If it has any object it must be to scare the contractor. As it stands, however, it seems to me that failure to get the certificate precludes operation.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The registered certificate is required solely for statistical purposes.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Section 13 states that failure to obtain the certificate is punishable by fine of $10 for each day during which such failure continues. That is quite plain. If it is not the intention to prevent operations on this account, then I say that section 5 must be amended; because as it stands it distinctly prevents any work being done:	It says that no distribution system "shall" be operated until certificate is obtained.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Perhaps it
might meet the difficulty and be perfectly clear if the section read:
Every distribution system for supplying- gas to any purchaser shall obtain from the minister a certificate of registration for such system.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: What is the particular reason for requiring an annual application for registration? Once a gas company has registered would that not be quite sufficient? These concerns are not like some small affair; the contractors cannot put them on their backs and walk off with them.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: It would be rather difficult for them to put the gas system into their pockets and go away with them, but still a company might go out of business, and it is well to have the registration complete in the office. Besides, it entails no hardship.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
The clause now
reads:
Every distribution system for supplying gas to any purchaser shall first obtain from the minister a certificate of registration for such system.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
The word
"first" should not be there.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Supposing a contractor is supplying gas and at the end of the year he fails to obtain a certificate?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
He gets his
certificate as a matter of course, as long as he has a system in operation.
Section as amended agreed to.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Mr. Bureau now
moves that the committee refer to clause 3 of the Bill. Shall clause 3 as amended carry?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I renew my objections.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The hon. gentleman's point is provided for in section 19 which we will come to later.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: In connection with this clause may I ask my right hon. friend if provision is made elsewhere in the Bill for the speedy publication of these Orders in Council that are passed? The Bill is of such general application and of such importance, that it seems to me necessary that the different Orders in Council which may be passed under this section should become speedily known.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Copies of the Orders in Council are distributed immediately to each company direct from the office.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: May it not be a matter of general interest that the Orders in Council should be published in the Canada Gazette, for instance, within a certain time after the Orders are passed?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
The Order in
Council affects the contractor and he gets a copy of it. The departmental officer thinks that no good purpose would be gained by carrying out my friend's suggestion. It would only be another cause of expense and we are so economical these days.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I do not think section 19, to which my right hon. friend referred, meets the case. It does not appear to me that the provisions are such as to give sufficient protection to the consumer. '

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I understand the question has been raised as to whether the power to act in this matter belongs to the Dominion, or whether it is a question of provincial and municipal regulation.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I do not see that there would be any danger to the public interest if we were to preserve the language of the

old Act. It has been in effect since 1910 and I do not think its authority has ever been disputed.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I am informed that on two or three occasions cases have been taken to Court and we have lost them.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I would like the right hon. gentleman to cite me one of those cases in respect to gas.
Section as amended agreed to.
On Section 6-right of access by contractor to premises where gas is used.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Paragraph (c) gives
the contractor the power to enter the premises of a purchaser for the purpose of changing or removing any piping, et cetera. That seems to me to be a kind of arbitrary power to confer.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: But the contractor will be responsible for repairs.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
That is all very well
but some times a person would prefer not to be deprived of gas even if he obtained damages. It is provided that the contractor shall be responsible for any damage done, but he can take the piping away and leave the consumer without gas-in fact he may do it summarily. If it were provided that it might be done for certain reasons, or under certain conditions it would afford better protection for the consumer.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The clause as introduced here is new only as relates to gas inspection. It has been in force for the last twenty years in the inspection of electricity and no difficulty has been experienced under it.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
The two systems are
not the same in character and therefore you cannot compare them. Although they give the same results, that is to say they yield power, heat and light, the two systems are absolutely different.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I know they are different, but in both cases contractor has to go inside the house to install the apparatus.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
But I maintain that the two cases are not on all fours. There is nothing in the Act concerning electricity that gives a contractor power to go into another person's house and rip up floors in order to put in wiring. Unless it is a matter of contract as between the parties,
the company, in the case of electricity stops at the outside wall and provides you with the current there.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I do not think my hon. friend's fears are justified as to what injury may be done.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I have not got any
fears.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Experience is the best test in a matter of this kind.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I do not believe in waiting until the horse is stolen before locking the stable.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: If a pipe gets out of order and the contractor is responsible he ought to have the right of entry and the right to make good the damage which exists inside and prevents the system from working.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: To say that the contractor can enter a house and remove any piping is a little hard.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Mr. Bureau moves: that clause 6 be amended by striking out the words "or removing" in the fortieth line. Shall the amendment carry?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Does the provision in clause (c) mean that the inspector may enter a gas field and remove any of the regulators and so stop the pressure of gas to the public?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: If the owner of the building or house con\es to the conclusion that he will not take any more gas, the contractor will have the right to enter and remove his fixtures.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: He has already at law full remedy to get back what belongs to him. I do not see why we should give him this drastic power of entering and ripping out pipes and meters.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Is not an hon. member of this group entitled to have his question answered so that he can hear the. answer?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Will the inspector have the right to enter a private building and remove the piping or interfere with a line supplying a village with gas by removing a meter or cutting a pipe without consulting the consumer or consumers?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: It is the contractor.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Would he have that right without giving notice to the public?

The reason I ask this question is because in my immediate vicinity last fall a whole village was cut off by a certain gas company removing the pressure ipeter, and the people were in darkness and suffered a good deal of inconvenience in consequence; in fact, the lighthouses along the lake were out.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I submit that this right should be left entirely to the contract or agreement that the selling of gas makes with the purchaser. They have their private contract, and one of its terms should be that the contractor has the right to go in and remove his property from any building, or to go in and repair that property; but I think it is rather arbitrary for us to make a one-sided contract and give the contractor this unlimited power.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Is the Committee
ready for the question? Sir George Foster moves that clause 6 do carry. Mr. Bureau moves an amendment to strike out the words "or removing" in the fortieth line.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Before you put the motion, Mr. Chairman-

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I am very sorry, but I must remind the hon. member that the motion was put for the' second time. The Committee was asked if it was ready for the question, and no answer came. I am sure the hon. gentleman's remarks will be quite relevant after the motion is put.
Amendment (Mr. Bureau) negatived.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I was going to speak on the amendment, Mr. Chairman, but as it has been declared lost I have nothing more to say.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Has the Minister considered-

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
If my hon.
friend will allow me? I think we had better be a little careful before we strike this out of the Bill as it has been very carefully prepared by officers who have had this matter under their charge for many years, and they have brought down to the House what they consider is necessary for the proper carrying out of the Act. I have been speaking with the inspector, and if the clause be considered somewhat drastic in its present form, as stated by my hon. friend from North Cape Breton (Mr. McKenzie), it might be made perfectly reasonable by the addition of this phrase:
The contractor may at all reasonable hours and with the consent of the purchaser. . .

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Since my hon. friend from East Elgin (Mr. McDermand) has taken the floor I think my case is far stronger. Supposing gas is being supplied to me and to another consumer through a common pipe, and the company wish to cut off his supply by tearing out a piece of pipe not only my house but the house of the man whom they wanted to deprive of gas will be shut off. Why should the contractor come on the premises and tear out the pipe? My hon. friend says that it is the contractor's property. But the contractor is entitled to replevy that property at any time. I think a county court judge is much better equipped to try each particular case than we are to lay down a general law empowering a contractor at any time to enter and remove piping. My right hon. friend may change the wording of the clause, but the removal of the piping is the objectionable feature.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: It was the questioi of removal that affected the village oi which I spoke. The company removed tht generator in that case and the whole village was in darkness and subject to the weather. I think the consumer should have certain notice given him before changes or removals are made.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Who did it in that case?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The Dominion Gas Company.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
The amendment was
declared lost.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
The amendment to
strike out the words "or removing" from clause (c) was lost, but any other amendment striking out the entire paragraph or amending it in any way except deleting the words "or removing" would. be in order.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: It might be pointed out that this section, at all events as I understand it, does not confer on a man the right to remove piping; it is for the purpose of giving him a right to enter the premises.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: For what purpose?

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Supposing that that man had a lawful right to remove piping. If you strike out the words "or removing", then he would not have the right to enter the premises. The purpose, as I understand it, is_ not to determine whether the contractor has the right to remove any piping, but when he has that right, to determine whether he shall have the right to enter at any reasonable hour for the purpose of exercising his right of removal. I would

suggest that instead of striking out the words "or removing" we insert after "removing" the words, "when lawfully entitled so to do". I should think there would be no objection to adding these words.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The Minister will see the difficulty which is there introduced. Who is to decide what is a lawful right?

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: My own interpretation of the section is that it confers a right to enter, not a right to remove; but where a man has a right to remove, this section gives him a right to enter. Nobody can decide then and there whether or not he has a right to remove; that necessarily would have to be fought out afterwards. Suppose a man had a judgment of the court determining that he had a right to remove, and the occupant barred the door.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: He could go to the sheriff.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: He might have to go to the sheriff; but why, in cases where the right to remove is not disputed or disputable should there not be a right to enter?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
The purposes for
which the contractor may enter are clearly defined in the section. It provides first that he may enter; then it sets forth what he may do after he gets in. Now, if it is objectionable that he should go in and do all these things, we should not allow him to go in. So far as I am familiar with the operations of electric concerns-and they are about the same thing; one supplies light and the other gas-the local Acts give them authority to put up poles, string their wires, and all that sort of thing, but the matter of what happens between the purchaser and the contractor as respects what the contractor shall do in the purchaser's house is the subject of private agreement between them. Perhaps we might well leave it to themselves to make such arrangements as might be thought proper in this regard, instead of making an unilateral contract-telling a contractor what he may do, and offering no protection to the purchaser, the man who owns the house. Then, I think the caption of this section is somewhat deceiving-"Inspection."	If these
things were done by a qualified inspector, I would have no objection, because he would be a good man, interested in both parties. But this is not an inspection; it is conferring power on the owner of the plant to do certain things. I do not quite understand why it comes under the head of "inspection."

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I agree with the remarks of the hon. member (Mr. McKenzie).
I cannot help feeling, upon reading the whole section and the caption of it, that whoever drafted the clause intended to make sub-section (c) read this way:
Changing or improving any piping, fittings, meters or other apparatus belonging to the contractor.
That, to my mind, is a reasonable view to take of the section; any other view is quite out of keeping with the rights of the public in dealing with large corporations supplying gas. If, on the other hand, it should be said that my view in this regard is not correct, I would simply fall in with the amendment of the Minister of Justice (Mr. Doherty) by adding to it these words: "after three days' notice to the occupant," so that paragraph (c) would read:
changing or removing, when lawfully entitled so to do, after three days' notice to the occupant, any piping, fittings, meters or other apparatus belonging to the contractor.
So that if a person is aggrieved by arbitrary or captious pressure on the part of an incorporated company, amounting, in his opinion, to infringement upon his personal rights, he would have three days within which to apply to the court for an injunction to restrain the removal and thereby get redress before the damage is actually done.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I can hardly agree with my hon. friend. As to what the member for North Cape Breton says about the word "inspection," I may point out that the inspection is by the contractor's inspector, not by the provincial inspector or whoever the province employs. As to the words "removing any piping, fittings, meters" and so on, you have to give the contractor permission to remove piping because if the purchaser has not been paying his bills or for some other reason the contractor thinks it necessary to remove the meter, he could not do so without at the same time removing a certain amount of piping. I do not see how we can refuse to allow the contractor to do what is necessary to the carrying on of his business in a business-like way. He should not be asked to supply gas to people who do not pay for it. I think that the clause, taken with sub-section 2, which makes the company responsible for damage, is all right as it stands, because I do not believe any contractor or supplier of gas is going to remove piping or meters unless such ac-

tion is necessary, because he is not being paid for the gas, or has some other good reasons of that kind. These men are out to do business, just the same as anybody else, and unless they are selling at a loss -and that is not likely-the more gas they can sell the better for them.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I should like the attention of the hon. member for Three Rivers (Mr. Bureau) to what I am about to suggest because I think we have been talking about this under a misapprehension; at least I know I have. This does not purport to give the right of forcible entry. It establishes the fact that a man has a right to go in to do all those things that are enumerated. If I am a tenant in possession and I do not think he has any right to do the things that he proposes to do when he enters my residence, I will simply barricade my door. He will not have any right of forcible entry; to enforce his right of entry, he will have to go to the court, and then we shall thresh out the question whether he has a right to do those things which he says he wants to enter to do. I do not think anybody is exposed to any forcible action, because the' law simply says that the man has a right of entry for certain purposes, and I think we can take it for granted that his right of entry is only subject to his being in a position lawfully to do those things. I do not think anybody suffers any great danger under this clause.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
The Minister of Justice (Mr. Doherty) knows as well as I do that when a company is getting a charter to supply gas, it is careful to see that everything is put in that is necessary for the protection of its rights. By this clause we are giving a man, who is not under the control of the Federal Government, certain powers as regards his contract with another man who owns a house. If you were saying that the inspector should go in. I would say:	"All
right; this is one of your own officers, and it is up to you to legislate as to your officers". But you say, "The contractor." My right hon. friend says: "What we want by this clause is the right to enter the premises;" but where has the contractor a right to read the meter, except by this section? Where has he a right to take it away, except by this section? My objection is that we step in and say that the contractor shall do certain things. The contractor is not our officer. He may have his charter from the Dominion Government, as is the case with the Ottawa Gas company; he may get it from a provincial legislature, and in his charter all the powers of the contractor

are well defined and enumerated and I think those who look after the contractor are careful, when they ask for a charter, to see that all necessary powers are granted. Why then, should we give additional powrs to a contractor, such as the removal of pipes or entry at any time? Let the inspector go in and bring in the contractor if he pleases, but I object to the contractor or his servant being given the right to enter my house and to remove pipes or to do the other things that are enumerated.
As regards the clause relating to damages, I have only to mention the word "damages" to the Minister of Justice to make him smile. He knows as well as I do that very often when we go before the courts to get damages, the costs of the action exceed the compensation received. I might call that section a section of frivolity, because it does not amount to anything.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I think we are going
far beyond the purview of this legislation when we are dealing with property end civil rights. At an early stage of the discussion this afternoon the question was raised as to our right to go into the provinces at all to deal with matters of this kind. The minister quite properly answered that the question of weights and measures comes within the jurisdiction of this Parliament, and consequently we had a right to deal with weights and measures. But clause 6 goes far beyond that; it tells a man who owns a house what shall happen; that a certain contractor may enter his house, and may do certain things. That is dealing with property and civil rights and has nothing to do with weights and measures. If we say that our inspector can go in and examine a house and do what ever is necessary for the purpose of the Bill, I will say that that is incidental to the jurisdiction of weights and measures; but I ask the Minister of Justice; By what authority can we deal in this Bill with property and civil rights? This is a question of property within a province, and we are telling a man he can go in and do practically what he pleases with that property. 1 do not think that comes within the scope of this legislation.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Listening to this debate, I felt that the matters covered by this clause are rather trifling and unimportant to be included in a Dominion Act, and I want to supplement what my hon. friend (Mr. McKenzie) has said by suggesting to the Minister of Justice (Mr. Doherty) and the

Minister of Trade and Commerce (Sir George Foster) that the matter might very well be left to contract between individuals. Would that not be covered in such cases by the ordinary arrangements that are made in regard to matters of this kind, making it unnecessary for us to incorporate it in an Act of Dominion application?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: As regards the amendment moved by the Minister of Justice, is the contractor not lawfully entitled to enter when he is given the right of access?

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
If anybody objects to
my amendment I have no desire to press it. Personally, I do not think it is necessary. I think, that with the exception of the right to enter, this clause does not confer substantial rights on anybody who has not those rights already.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Strike it out.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: As regards the sub-amendment " after three days' notice to the occupants," that might act very badly; gas might be escaping, running all through a house, poisoning everybody, or it might catch fire and burn up the whole place.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I am sure, if gas were
escaping, no objection would be raised to the contractor coming in and stopping the leak. What I wish to provide against is an arbitrary entry, when no gas was escaping, in order to take away pipes that are useful, not that are useless.
Amendment agreed to.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: What is the real purpose of this clause in any event? In the first place, every gas company, before it can supply gas will have a franchise from a municipality, and under that franchise it will have rights that should be sufficient for it. I^hy should the Dominion Government be passing this legislation, and particularly this clause, when they have all these rights already under their franchise; and if not, why should we give them rights which the municipal franchise would not give.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I should like
to consult the officers of the Department before I make a decision, and I therefore move that further consideration of this section be postponed.

Motion agreed to. Section stands.
On section 7-pressure:

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
This clause provides
that "The contractor shall from time to
time report to the minister what the minimum service pressure is and shall provide, free of charge, etc., etc." We have had a great deal of trouble in Western Ontario over gas this last year. Some corporations have complained that there is not enough pressure, and others that the gas is poisonous and smells too much, and they have had the provincial Railway Board and a gas inspector up there investigating. There has been a lot of trouble between the municipalities and the gas companies, and my question is: where does the Dominion Government's authority come in, and where does the Provincial Government s authority come in? The same question applies to section 6, which has been allowed to stand. If the two authorities clash, I should like to know exactly where they do clash, because this is a very vexed question up in Western Ontario, and is causing constant rows between the municipalities and the gas companies.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The purpose of this clause is to put the department in possession of a fact, as to what the pressure really is. We have no power, and this does not give us power, to say what the pressure shall be.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: If you have no authority to do anything, what is the good of having the knowledge?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The knowledge of what the pressure is, is necessary to us in testing the meters, and that is the whole purpose for which this clause exists. The pressure may be high or low, and in order to make an accurate test we have to know just what the pressure is.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Then we have no authority to control the gas companies?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: We cannot say what the pressure shall be.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Or what the supply shall be?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: You have to go to your municipality for that.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: This is a new clause. How have the companies and the authorities been getting along hitherto without it? The minister does not give any good reason why it should be inserted.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I think the reason I have given is a good one. If we want a piece of information for the purpose of carrying out our work, we ought to be able to get that information.

We are not responsible for the fact of what the pressure is, but we are responsible for testing the meters, and we simply want to get the fact as to the pressure, in order that we may do our work in conformity with that fact.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Just what is the work of the department?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The work of the department in so far as this is concerned, is to get information upon which to test the meters. The pressure may be high or it may be low. Now the meter has to be tested according to the pressure, and we simply want to know the fact of what the pressure is. This very same provision has been in force with respect to the inspection of electricity for the very same purpose.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
No doubt the minister has a perfect right to test the pressure, because that is incidental to the real purpose of the inspection, but I have very grave doubts whether he has power to compel the contractor to furnish the tools for doing that.
toST GE0RGE FOSTER: It is not the

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Has the minister received any information from the gas companies throughout the Dominion as to how this will affect their operations? We have natural gas in the city of Moncton. It is piped seven or eight miles into the city and then distributed. Sometimes the gas has been reported pretty low. Has the minister conferred with the companies who will be affected by this legislation.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: My hon. friend will see that this will not interfere with any company which is piping gas into a city. It merely asks that company: Please be kind enough to tell us what your pressure is, as we want the information in order to test the meters. That does not affect the company's operation.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Except that they have to supply the pipe and facilities for the test.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: That is only a neighbourly thing for them to do.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: How will these tests be made, and to what expenses will the companies be put in supplying these facilities? I should like some information on these points.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: It is the apparatus then. You are saying to the contractor We want to make tests, and we are goinj o make you supply the necessary machinery to make our tests. Now I have very grav< doubts whether you have any right to saj that to any contractor. I have very grave doubts whether you can compel him tc keep extra apparatus for that purpose

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: It has always been done m connection with the inspection. Do not put it into their heads that we have no right to do it.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Is this c ause new? What has been the procedure in the past?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The meter has to be tested under the existing conditions, and one of those conditions is the amount of the pressure. We want to know just what that pressure is, for without that knowledge we cannot fairly test the meters.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: What has been the practice in the past?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The officer tells me they have simply had to take their chances in testing the meters, and that it has been very unsatisfactory.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: This really means a saving to the companies because, instead of asking them to bring their meters to be inspected at the office of the inspector, our meters are taken to the premises and all the company is asked to do is to connect up a pipe to help the inspector in making the test.

Section agreed to. ,
On section 8-Director.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
This seems to be a radical
departure from the Acts of 1906 and 1910. We seem to be appointing a new' director and new officers, and you are taking great powers to yourselves. You are appointing numerous inspectors and assistants. What is the reason for this change, and what will the additional cost be?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I am glad to
be able to tell my hon. friend that this does not contemplate, nor does it provide for, the appointment of a single additional officer. It merely gives the names and the powers of officers already at work.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
It seems to me that the caption of the clause is rather misleading when read in connection with section 6. Section 6 is headed "Inspection." To my mind it should be headed "Directors' rights

and privileges." Section 8 is headed "Officers" and deals with inspection. The caption should indicate the purport of the clause. Then they would not be misleading the people who wished to understand the law.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: This deals with the appointment of officers.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: For inspection purposes. Sir GEORGE FOSTER:	Yes.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
And the one that deals
with directors' right is headed "Inspection".
It seems so abnormally out of place that I thought I would mention it.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I would draw attention
to sub-clause 4. Does not the Civil Service Act as it now stands provide for this qualifying examination? Why insist on introducing it into this legislation?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I think the
provisions of the Civil Service Act cover this case, but perhaps it might be just as well to let it stand.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
As I understand the
Civil Service Act, all these positions in all departments are filled by examination, and I think it unwise to introduce into this Act or any other Act a special clause with reference to examination.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Is it not a fact that by
Order in Council the Government can at any time over-ride this provision with regard to examination, as they have done in connection with the census Enumerators and the Purchasing Board?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I move to
strike out sub-section 4.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: What is the subsection?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: It provides what is already provided under the Civil Service Act.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I have the greatest
objection to striking out anything that has any tendency to remind the Government that there is such a thing as the Civil Service Act, because it should be kept before them continually. They should be reminded of it at every turn of the road. It is bad enough as it is, but if nothing is said in the House or in bills about the Civil Service Act the Governement will forget all about it.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: My hon. friend is quite wrong.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
My hon. friend (Mr. Cahill) has just brought to the attention of the Government the fact that officials under the census regulations have been appointed regardless of the Civil Service Act. I do not quite understand why that should be so. Surely this is a matter that ought to come within the operations of the Act. These officers do Government work of a very important character, and why should not the Government ask the Civil Service Commission to submit to them a list of men in the different counties of Canada capable of doing this work? Other matters of less importance are submitted to the Civil Service Commission, but here was a very large slice of patronage and the Civil Service Commission was put aside. The old Tory machine is renovated and put into running order, and the appointees are absolutely and entirely of the old school. I have had the opportunity of looking at the Halifax papers this morning in which the officers in my own county and others in the province are given, and I can assure my right hon. friend that they will pass the acid test of Toryism of the finest order. In mentioning this I am not finding fault, because if I had power and the Civil Service Act were outmf the way I would do exactly the same thing. But I do object to the camouflage of affirming that there is a Civil Service Act in this country under which we are supposed to select officers through a commission appointed for the purpose, while at the same time we find the Government over-riding that Act. I think the minister at this very stage should define as clearly as he can where the Civil Service Act is in this legislation, so that henceforth we shall know when there is a transgression of that Act.
I should like to have some explanation from the minister. Perhaps it does not come within the scope of this discussion as to why he as one of the ministers of the Crown has ignored-if such is the case-the Civil Service Act in connection with the census. Why should the appointments be made regardless of the provisions of that Act?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: We shall have ample time no doubt on a more fitting occasion to take up that particular question and discuss it. It really has nothing to do with the use of gas or the work of testing meters or anything of that nature. There will be an answer for my hon. friend at the proper time and I hope he will restrain his impatience until then.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I do not think this clause should be struck out. If we leave

the matter entirely in the hands of the Civil Service Commission they may determine that an examination is not necessary, and may dispense with it in making these appointments. Now, where we are dealing with gas, something which is very essential and at the same time very dangerous, I think there should be the statutory requirement that no persons should be appointed to these positions until they have passed a technical examination. This clause simply makes it obligatory that there shall be a technical examination under the direction of the Civil Service Commission. I do not think it would be wise to leave it in the hands of the Commission to say whether or not there should be a technical examination, or any examination at all, and give the Commission power to make the appointment without deciding' whether the applicants for these positions are techncially qualified to fill them.

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Minister presiding over the Department of Health; President of the Privy Council
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I am inclined to think there is a point in the argument of the hon. member for Calgary (Mr. Tweedie). As I understand the Civil Service law, appointments to the Civil Service are certified by the Civil Service Commission either with or without examination, the matter being left to their judgment as to whether an examination is necessary or not. It seems to me that in cases of officials of this character there should be an examination.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I would suggest to the Minister of Immigration and Colonization this fact: This clause gives the Civil Service Commission absolute power to prescribe the nature of the examination, but it does not state that it shall be of a certain type. It says " such examination to be held under the direction of the Civil Service Commission." I submit the whole thing is covered by the Civil Service Act, and this is a perfectly useless clause.
_ Sir GEORGE FOSTER: There are two sides to that question and I am not sure but that the suggestion of my hon. friend back of me (Mr. Tweedie) should be taken into consideration. It is just possible-
I ^ think it may be more than that-the Civil Service Commission under the powers given to them by the Act may appoint these officers without examination. Now, the purpose of inserting this clause is'-tnat in reference to these officers there shall be an examination provided for by 
the Civil Service Commission, and that they shall be appointed by the Commission only after a technical examination. If that me so, if it is absolutely essential that technical acquirements shall be the basis for the appointment of officers to these positions, and that seems to be the case, the clause should remain. Under the circumstances I will ask that further discussion of the matter be postponed, and the section be held for the time being.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Shall the minister have the right to withdraw his amendment?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I certainly think
that subsection 4 of section 8 is important and should remain. We know that the Civil Service Commission now appoint parties to the public service from year to year without an examination at all, and call such appointments temporary. If it it imperative that no person should be appointed to a position such as is provided for here without passing a technical examination then the section should remain.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The amendment is withdrawn, shall the clause carry?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The minister stated that there were to be no new appointments, and yet the very first clause of the Bill provides for the appointment of a director.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: That is, an officer who is already existent and performing the duties shall be made director, that is all. The statement I made is correct.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: And there is to be no change in the salary?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: No change in the salary and no change in the number of officers.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Am I right in understanding from the minister that the appointment of a director and inspectors will be made by the Civil Service Commission?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
The existing
Civil Service Act brings the appointment of these officers under the Civil Service Commission. The only point which has been raised is this: the Civil Service Commission may appoint to an office either with or without an examination. The department takes the view that with reference to these officers there must always be a technical examination. That is the reason we

have put this clause in the Act, to make sure that the Civil Service Commission in appointing shall only appoint after an examination of the technical qualifications of the applicants.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: That may be the minister's view but if the section is taken as it is, it will be found to be possible for the Civil Service Commisson to have ten or fifteen men pass an examination and be pronounced qualified for these positions. Section 4 does not say that appointments will be made by the Civil Service Commission.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The Civil Service Act does that.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
But this section may
supersede the provisions of the Civil Service Act.	.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
The object of
this section is simply to make sure that there shall be a technical examination, which I think is perfectly right.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Does that mean that the
present officers shall have to take an examination, or is the examination only to apply to new officers that may be appointed from time to time?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I presume it
applies to new officers only. The present officers are qualified.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I would ask the minister if he considers the wording of subsection 3 of section 8 sufficiently definite. We are now framing this Bill, and I think we should make it a little more specific in certain details. The provision to which I have particular reference declares that an officer may at all reasonable hours enter any premises. Now we should define what we consider "reasonable hours" to be and not leave the matter open. The same, or similar, phraseology occurs in section 6. I think we should define what we mean by "reasonable hours," and I would suggest that we say between the hours of 9 a.m. and 5 p.m.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: There might be something occurring at the other hours to prevent the officer from carrying out the duty. I think my hon. friend will find it very difficult to go further in the matter of definition than is set out in the Bill. Circumstances must determine the hour.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
But there may be two
opinions as to what constitutes "reasonable hours." A moment ago in the discussion of this Bill we had a difference of opinion
upon certain matters, and it is equally possible that there will be a difference of opinion in regard to the present point. I certainly think we should settle details of this kind when we are framing the Bill.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I do not think we could make the provision more specific than it is.

Section agreed to.
On section 9-meters, etc:

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Will not the provisions of this clause interfere with the ordinary employees of a gas company? By this clause it would seem to me that no inspector outside of the one nominated by the Government, or the Civil Service Commission, would have the right to enter houses and verify the meters, although at the present time the gas companies' employees perform this work.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: We do not interfere with the employees of the company which is furnishing the gas.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Subsection 9 reads:
Within six years from each verification and sealing every meter shall be presented by the owner for re-verification and re-sealing, or for the cancellation of the seal by the inspector.
There is no definition under this Act of what constitutes an owner, but there is a definition of what	constitutes
a contractor-the person who supplies the gas. Invariably the contractors supply the meters, and in my experience they rent those meters and will not sell them. Now, it seems to me from the point of view of public right that the duty under sub-section 5 should be cast upon the contractor, the man who supplies the gas, to provide at his own expense for the re-verification of the meters at that period of time when they should be verified. The word "owner" in used in the subsection. There may be a way of getting around that by the contractor saying he leased the meter, or in some other way he may say that he is not the owner; I cannot say what might happen under the interpretation that might be given to the clause; but I think the word "contractor" should be put into that section specifically and that the duty should be cast upon him of arranging and paying for the re-verification of the meters periodically.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
There are cases in which the contractor or the company does not own the meters, they are owned by the consumers themselves; and this subsection makes it necessary for either owner,

whether it be the consumer or the company, to have the re-verification carried out.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: If that is certain, I am . satisfied.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Under this clause there does not seem to be any protection thrown around the public in regard to when the meter should be verified. In the old Act of 1906 by section 19 it is provided:
No meter shall he stamped which is found by the inspector to register, or capable of being made to register, quantities varying from the true standard measure of gas, more than three per centum in favour of the seller, or four per centum in favour of the consumer.
But there seems to be nothing m this Bill protecting the consumer in that regard. Why was this protection left out?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I am told that the inspector of the department has the power to order the re-verification of a meter at any time if it is found to be defective, but that all meters under this general clause must be re-verified every six years.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The minister does not quite get my point. Under the Act of 1906, and also under the later Act of 1910, there are standards set up to protect the public; but under this Bill there is no provision at all in that regard.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: There is a provision in this Bill by which the standard shall be set by Order in Council, and the officer works under that Order in Council.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: Why should it be done by Order in Council now when it has never been done heretofore in that way; why not by statute?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The reason is that if it is in the Act, every time you changed the standard you would have to enact fresh legislation. These changes of standard take place from time to time, and it is conducive to the best operation that they shall be adopted without loss of time. The same amount of protection is afforded under this Bill, but added protection is given as according to experience we change the fineness of the standard.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
I do not quite follow the minister's explanation. I cannot conceive that the fineness of standard would vary so rapidly that we could not establish a basis in the . statute to protect the consumer. From the fact that the standard established in 1906 was not changed in the Act of 1910, I would assume that the standards do not vary very rapidly, and even if we

had to pass legislation I think the public would be much more satisfied to depend on a statutory provision rather than on an Order in Council which might or might not be passed.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: These gentlemen have a habit of passing Orders in Council.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
The officers of the department think it would be better to have the section remain in its present form.
On section 10-tests in the case of disputed accuracy of meter:

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: This is just the same as the old Act, except that it is a little more definitely stated.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: There were many rules in the old Act with respect to testing which I do not find in this Bill. Why were thev left out?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: They will be provided for, as I said before, in regulations passed by Order in Council, and for the same reason.

Section agreed to.
On Section 16-for not keeping records or permitting inspection of them:

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: I move that the words "not exceeding" be inserted after the word "of" in the fourth line.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: All right-the penalty not to be less than five dollars.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
Mr. McKenzie moves to amend clause 16 by adding after the word "of" in the fourth line thereof, the following words: "of not less than five and not more than,"
so that the clause will read:
shall be liable to a penalty of not less than five and not more than fifty dollars.

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: What is to get the bene fit of the penalty, the Crown, or the mar who prosecutes?

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext: The Crown.

Amendment agreed to, and section is amended agreed to.
On section 19-for supplying injurious gas:

maintopic: INSPECTION OF GAS AND GAS METERS
speechtext:
In the old Act there is a section which has a very important effect on the part of the country from which I come. It provides that:
The supply of gas shall be regular and sufficient.

The old Act distinctly provides that a company shall give a sufficient supply of gas, when they have the gas to give to the consumer.
